A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe the same Words in Motion study. Text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A.1–A.19 support comparison, including matching reordered appendix material.

before.justification: v4 reports original motion-feature probing, control-vector evaluations, ablations and zero-shot forecasting results on AV2F and Waymo.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds a qualitative demonstration of steering all agents in Figure 15.

M1.justification: Motion-feature quantization, linear probing, PCA pooling, SAE optimization and temperature-scaled activation steering remain unchanged. The all-agent illustration uses the existing method.

E1.justification: The AV2F and Waymo datasets, agent types, forecasting/control tasks and reduced-speed domain-shift evaluation are retained. New Figure 15 illustrates all-agent steering within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated motion models and plain-PCA, SAE, SparseMLPMixer, ConvSAE and KoopmanAE comparisons are unchanged. Cunningham et al. changes from a 2023 preprint citation to its 2024 publication, without changing the comparator.

E3.justification: New Figure 15 adds a qualitative testing setup with a default forecast and all-agent steering at eight temperatures from -100 to 100. Existing quantitative protocols remain unchanged. Replacing 'cosine similarity in degrees' with angular-distance terminology clarifies unchanged degree-valued tables.

E4.justification: Appendix A.8 adds a case study showing simultaneous steering of all agents across temperatures. Existing module and speed-threshold ablations, feature-correlation analyses and calibration comparisons are retained, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including latency means over 1,000 iterations. No new seed information, uncertainty intervals or significance tests accompany the added qualitative example.

E6.justification: Figure 15 adds qualitative trajectory outcomes described as consistent multi-agent behavior. Existing numerical results are unchanged after matching reordered tables, including SAE-128 linearity scores of 0.993 Pearson, 0.984 R2 and 0.988 straightness in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), the CDNV definition in Appendix A.19 and the underlying mathematical assumptions remain unchanged. The angular-distance wording corrects terminology without introducing a new definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about interpretable representations, control vectors, SAE-enhanced linearity and zero-shot generalization. The edited third contribution bullet preserves its original scientific scope.

C2.justification: Explanations involving feature separability, sparsity and activation shrinkage remain unchanged, as do the flat-latent-space and limited neural-collapse-analysis qualifications. Figure 15 adds an observed outcome without a new mechanism explanation or substantive limitation.

D1.justification: Implementation information, training hyperparameters, classification thresholds and the code-access link are unchanged. Hardware and profiling details move with the latency experiment from Appendix A.10 to A.11 without substantive revision.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Cunningham et al. and DriveLM receive preprint-to-conference bibliographic updates; these are the same works, not additions to the literature comparison.

P1.justification: v5 corrects angular-distance terminology, lightly rewrites the third contribution bullet and reorders Appendix A.9–A.16 with updated cross-references. The main narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds the nine-panel Figure 15, adjusts Figure 14's framing and size, revises comparison-table captions and relocates several appendix displays. Existing figures and tables are retained with corresponding renumbering.

improvement.justification: Correcting the misleading 'cosine similarity in degrees' terminology improves clarity, while Figure 15 provides useful qualitative support for simultaneous steering. The method and quantitative evidence remain unchanged, so these benefits constitute a limited overall improvement.
